biography.plain_text: Gianpiero Moretti was an Italian entrepreneur and racing driver who founded MOMO, the international automotive accessories business. Born into a prosperous Milanese family, he built the company around steering wheels before expanding into alloy wheels and road-car equipment. His family sold its remaining MOMO stake to Breed Technologies in 1996.

long_biography.plain_text:
Automotive entrepreneur and MOMO founder Gianpiero Moretti helped persuade Ferrari to build the 333 SP, a sports prototype intended for endurance racing. He had spent much of his own racing career in Porsches, yet wanted to compete again in a Ferrari. In 1998 he shared victories at Daytona, Sebring and Watkins Glen, completing a sweep of three major American endurance races before finally retiring from driving.

The paddock also knew Moretti as a host. He cooked spaghetti in the garage for competitors and journalists, turning race meetings into informal gatherings. His public-relations colleague Barbara Burns remembered that these dinners made guests feel included in his life.

uncertainties: Research cutoff 30 September 2026; sources accessed 1 October 2026. For this deceased person, primary industry and wealth relationship refer to the terminal position in January 2012, not the activities or wealth of heirs and subsequent company owners.

Identity is convergent rather than based on one source supplying full name, company and vessel: Florida DOR establishes Dr. Moretti, Italian nationality, Fifty-One and late-1993 sale; the SunChaser build story establishes the racing-driver owner and fiftieth-birthday commission delayed into 1991. These align with the MOMO founder and the immutable vessel link. Input 1988 is earlier than completion; input age 71 as of 2020 is stale and is not used to calculate a birth date.

Gianpiero is the normal corporate and racing spelling; Giampiero is also used by contemporary reporting. Existing name and Dr. title are not overwritten. No medical profession is inferred from the honorific. The philosopher born in Rome in 1955, Quebec architect and living professional LinkedIn namesakes are different people.

The signed retrospective and reference biography give 20 March 1940, whereas the official ACO obituary gives 15 November 1944 in its full body. Official IMSA and the firsthand friend account give age 71 at death in 2012, independently supporting the stated 1940 year. The exact day/month are withheld as review candidates because that portion of the date conflict is unresolved.

Automotive is supported by a founded and substantially owned industrial platform. Its sales and the family's 40 percent disposal establish material operating scale and ownership without quantifying his individual stake or wealth. No enterprise total is treated as his net worth.

Broad Self-made rests on the positive creation, growth and ownership of MOMO. Wealthy family background and a pharmaceutical business are established; neither an inherited core nor the exact extent of materially enabling family support is established. The desire for financial independence is not proof that he started without substantial advantage.

The terminal sector uses the mandatory Automotive origin fallback. Full MOMO exit and presidency transfer are documented in 1996; later MomoDesign is Cattaneo's business. Mokart and racing ventures are positive later activity, but their ownership and scale within Moretti's 2012 assets are not established. Unknown relationship retains Founder as the strongest alternative without carrying forward a sold-company role.

The interview's Swiss passport statement explicitly concerns Moretti personally and contrasts nationality with his Italian cultural identity. It is not derived from Swiss family background or any vessel registration.

Forbes-first checks found no exact profile under either spelling. LinkedIn, Instagram and Personal Website were prioritised; Facebook, Twitter/X, Youtube and TikTok were then searched. No verified personal account was established. Corporate posts and historic racing footage are not personal channels; TikTok direct access is restricted.

Other supported link checks covered Wikipedia, Company Website, Vimeo, Flickr, Trip Advisor and Zillow. Historic Flickr photographs belong to photographers, not Moretti. The inaccessible memorial domain remains a candidate. The company history is proposed solely under Company Website because he founded MOMO, not as an indication of retained ownership.

Automotive components, Racing driver and Endurance racing capture separate industrial, practiced-role and sporting-discipline dimensions. Formula 1 is excluded: supplying drivers' equipment does not establish a defining competitive or governance F1 role. The broader Motorsport tag would overlap the narrower endurance discipline. Brief Baglietto ownership does not require an additional shipyard tag.

The short and long biographies are complementary historical accounts. The short reserves family background, product expansion and family stake disposal; the long supplies competition, prototype advocacy and social hospitality. Personal net worth and terminal holdings remain outside the prose.
